subject: dads who coach little league
tagline: PayPal for dads who coach little league
one_liner: Bunt is the payments platform for volunteer coaches who fronted $214 for pizza in April and are still owed $189 of it.
brand_voice_notes: Written like a regional bank that sponsors a Little League team and puts its logo on the outfield fence. Calm, procedural, a little wounded. Every feature is pitched as financial infrastructure for problems measured in orange slices, sunflower seeds and one umpire named Rick. The coach is always owed money. The coach is never paid back. Bunt treats this as a reconciliation issue and nothing more. Never mention feelings directly. Mention the clipboard.

hero.h1: Get paid back for the orange slices.
hero.sub: Bunt is payment infrastructure for the volunteer head coach. Request snack money, split the pizza by hustle, and dispute the team mom's Venmo note, all from the dugout, all before the 4:30 field permit expires.

features.title: Orange Slice Escrow
features.blurb: Snack parents pay into escrow on Thursday. Funds release on Saturday only after Bunt confirms, by photo, that the oranges were cut into eighths and not quarters. Quarters trigger a review.

features.title: Hustle-Weighted Splits
features.blurb: The post-game pizza is split by effort. Coaches grade each player from 1 to 10 on how fast they ran out a ground ball, and Bunt prices each slice accordingly. Kids who jogged pay full freight.

features.title: Clipboard Verification
features.blurb: Every payment over $6 requires the coach to hold a clipboard in frame. Our model has seen 41,000 clipboards. It knows a real clipboard from a cereal box with a binder clip.

pricing_tiers.name: Tee-Ball
pricing_tiers.tagline: For dads who said yes because nobody else raised a hand.
perks: Payouts settle in 3 to 5 business innings
Orange Slice Escrow (quarters only flagged, not refused)

pricing_tiers.name: Travel Ball
pricing_tiers.tagline: For dads who have called it a development year twice.
perks: Tournament hotel splits by bed, cot and floor
Automatic reminders sent to the team mom's husband

pricing_tiers.name: The Assistant Coach Wants Your Job
pricing_tiers.tagline: For dads who know exactly what Doug said in the parking lot.
perks: Chargebacks against the league board, filed in triplicate
A second clipboard, issued and insured
Priority dispute line staffed by a former umpire named Rick

testimonials.quote: I used to front the pizza money and never see it again. Now I front the pizza money and get a push notification confirming I will never see it again. That is closure.
testimonials.name: Greg Halvorsen
testimonials.title: Head Coach, Mud Hens 10U. Regional Sales Manager, Monday through Friday.

testimonials.quote: Hustle splits are fair. My own son paid $0.40 for his pizza last week. He also did not run to first. We discussed it in the car.
testimonials.name: Darnell Okafor
testimonials.title: Pitching Coordinator, Pirates (sponsored by Lou's Transmission & Tire)

testimonials.quote: Bunt held a $12 snack payment in escrow because the grapes were not cut in half. It was right to do that. I have told the Feldmans.
testimonials.name: Kevin Prusky
testimonials.title: First Base Coach, Bucket Carrier, Keeper of the Ball Bag

demo_screen_concept: The Bunt team ledger for the Mud Hens 10U, open on game day. A scorecard-style roster of 11 players, each row showing the parent, what they owe for snacks, pizza and the umpire tip, and a payment status chip (Paid, Pending, Owes, In Dispute). Each row has a hustle slider from 1 to 10; dragging it live-recomputes that family's share of the $86.40 pizza bill and the totals at the bottom. Filter chips across the top (All, Owes Coach, In Dispute, Paid), a fake search box for parent names, and a 'Request money' button that opens a modal where the coach picks a reason (orange slices, pizza, Rick's tip, replacement batting helmet), types an amount and a pencil-style memo, then sends it, which adds a line to the activity feed on the right ('Feldman, R. marked your request as seen').

design_direction.style: Retro ballpark scorecard, Saturday-morning daylight mode. A payments app printed like a 1970s minor-league program and the paper scorecard inside it: off-white card stock ground, navy ink ruled grids, red baseball-stitch seams, a varsity collegiate slab display face, and a coach's pencil handwriting scrawled in the margins. Explicitly absent, because the last seven entries used them: stud tiles, brass hairlines, velvet ropes, crests, gum leaf corners, sleep rings, zzz chips, 3px ink outlines with hard offset shadows, tennis seams, amount pills, masonry pins, iridescent gradients, crumb trails, lip buttons, lesson paths, bone meters, mascots, wall labels, empty plinths, clay stacks, silk threads, exuvia outlines. Also absent: dark backgrounds, glassmorphism, neon, blurred soft-UI shadows, rounded cards above 4px, Didone or bookish serifs. Four motifs carry the page. (1) The scorecard grid: features, tiers and the demo roster sit in a ruled navy grid of boxes, each with a small base-path diamond in the corner that fills in as an item is 'reached', like scoring a runner. (2) The stitch seam: a curved line of red V-stitches drawn as an SVG pattern separates sections and underlines the hero. (3) Coach's pencil: Kalam handwriting in graphite grey annotates the page ('ask Feldmans AGAIN', 'Rick = $20 cash'), slightly rotated, never more than one per section. (4) The pennant: the highlighted pricing tier and primary CTA badge use a felt-red triangular pennant shape. Corners 2px. Shadows: none, except a 1px navy rule offset 3px under cards like a second printed line.
design_direction.archetype: Hero-centric fintech landing composed as a ballpark program: masthead with issue number and price, hero, three-box scorecard feature row, testimonials as lineup cards, pricing as a three-column ticket stub row.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Diamonds fill base by base (four quick strokes, 60ms each) when a section enters view; stitch seams draw left to right once; pencil notes fade in with a 1.5 degree settle. All gated on a .js class with a timeout fallback, and disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Masthead strip at top ('BUNT · OFFICIAL PROGRAM · VOL. 1 NO. 1 · 25¢'). Left: huge Graduate h1 in navy over two lines with a red stitch seam underlining 'orange slices', sub and CTA below, a pencil note pointing at the CTA. Right: a program-cover photo of a coach on a dugout bench in a thin navy double-rule frame, captioned like a program photo ('Coach G. Halvorsen, owed $189'). Below the fold, the scorecard grid begins.

images.rationale: Hero used: the program-cover composition calls for a photo of the coach on the bench. Demo skipped: the ledger is a table with sliders, not photo-shaped, and generating images of children was avoided on purpose. Remaining 3 slots spent on deadpan bank-portrait headshots for the three named testimonials.

items.prompt: Editorial photograph in the style of a 1970s minor-league baseball program cover, slightly faded film color. A tired middle-aged dad volunteer little league coach sits alone on a wooden dugout bench, holding a clipboard, a bucket of baseballs beside him and a mesh bag of cut orange slices on the bench. Navy windbreaker, plain navy cap, whistle. Warm Saturday morning light, chain-link fence and dusty infield clay behind him, off-white cream tones #F4EFE1, navy #1E3560 and faded red #C7362B accents. Deadpan, sincere, slightly defeated expression. One focal subject. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no rendered UI screens, no writing on clothing or clipboard.

Deadpan corporate headshot photograph, like a regional bank employee portrait, of a pale, slightly sunburned white dad in his late forties with a short graying goatee, navy polo shirt, a volunteer little league baseball coach. Head and shoulders, centered, looking straight at camera with a polite tired expression. Plain flat cream backdrop #F4EFE1, soft even studio light, subtle navy #1E3560 in clothing only.
